Chris walked into the gym with the swagger of a man who had just watched one too many superhero movies. He spotted the new weight machine, a sleek piece of equipment that looked less like fitness gear and more like something from a sci-fi torture chamber. "Watch this," he muttered to no one in particular, adjusting his grip with the confidence of a seasoned bodybuilder.

He pulled the lever. Nothing happened. He pulled it harder. Still nothing. Then, in a move that can only be described as "aggressive hugging," he wrapped his arms around the machine, trying to wrestle it into submission. The machine, however, had other plans. It locked him in place, turning him into a very confused, very red-faced statue.

For the next thirty seconds, Chris was locked in an awkward embrace with the steel contraption, frantically patting its sides like he was trying to calm a spooked horse. He was searching for a release button that seemed to have gone into hiding. The nearby gym-goers didn't say a word, but the silence was loud with suppressed laughter. One woman actually dropped her water bottle trying to stifle a giggle. Chris finally found the button, popped free, and walked away with his dignity intact, though his face told a different story. It was a perfect showcase of man versus machine, and the machine won by a knockout.
